input: Hello BrachyBot, I am Dr. Sarah Chen from the radiation oncology department at Memorial Hospital. I have a new prostate cancer patient and I would like to start the brachytherapy planning process. Could you please introduce yourself and tell me what capabilities you have for helping me with this treatment plan?

Hi there! I am a medical physicist who just joined the brachytherapy team. I have never used an AI assistant for treatment planning before. What exactly can you do to help me with prostate LDR brachytherapy seed implant planning and quality assurance?

Good morning. This is Dr. Patel, a radiation oncologist. I need to evaluate a cervical cancer patient for HDR brachytherapy. I have a CT scan loaded and I want to know if you can help me with tandem and ovoid applicator planning. Please explain your workflow.

Hey, I am an intern at the cancer center. Dr. Kim asked me to run the brachytherapy bot for a breast cancer APBI case. I have never done this before. Can you walk me through what I need to do step by step?

Hello. I am a dosimetrist working on a complex head and neck interstitial brachytherapy case. The patient has a recurrent squamous cell carcinoma of the oral tongue. Can you assist me with the planning process from CT import to dose evaluation?
Hi BrachyBot, is this system connected to my treatment planning system or does it work independently? I want to understand the integration architecture before I start using it for patient cases.

Hello, I am reviewing a prostate brachytherapy preplan from another institution. The case uses I-125 seeds. I need to verify the plan quality. Can you load the CT and help me evaluate the dose coverage and hot spot locations?
Hi! I am conducting a research study on AI-assisted brachytherapy planning for endometrial cancer. I need to process 50 cases. Does this system support batch processing of multiple patients?

Good morning BrachyBot. I am a resident on my first rotation in brachytherapy. I would like to understand what imaging modalities you support. Can you work with MRI-only plans or do you require CT scans?

Hello. I represent the quality assurance committee at our cancer center. We are evaluating AI tools for brachytherapy. What validation studies have been performed on this system? How accurate is the automated segmentation compared to manual contouring?
Hey there. I have a bladder cancer case that needs HDR brachytherapy. The tumor is at the bladder dome. I have a CT scan ready. Can you help me plan this case using a single-channel technique?

Hi, I am a radiation safety officer. Before I allow this system to be used in our department, I need to understand what patient data is processed, where it is stored, and whether it complies with HIPAA regulations.
Good evening. I have an emergency case - a patient with massive vaginal bleeding from cervical cancer. We need to plan an urgent HDR brachytherapy session tonight. Can you help me plan quickly?

Hello BrachyBot. I am Dr. Tanaka from Japan. I would like to use this system but I have some questions about language support. Can you respond in Japanese? Does the system support multilingual interfaces?

Hi, I am a medical student doing a rotation in radiation oncology. I am writing a thesis on brachytherapy dose optimization. Can you help me understand the mathematical principles behind inverse planning for HDR prostate brachytherapy?

Good morning. I just received a CT scan of a patient with rectal cancer. I need to evaluate whether the patient is a candidate for endorectal brachytherapy boost. Can you analyze the CT and give me your assessment?
Hello. I am setting up a new brachytherapy program at a rural hospital. We have limited resources. Can this system help us plan cases even without a dedicated treatment planning system?
Hey BrachyBot! I am a physicist trying to commission a new HDR afterloader. Can you help me verify the source positioning accuracy by analyzing a phantom CT scan?

Hi there. I have a pediatric patient with a vaginal rhabdomyosarcoma who needs brachytherapy. This is a very delicate case. Can you help me plan it with appropriate organ-at-risk constraints for a child?
Good afternoon. I am the department director and I need a summary report of all brachytherapy cases planned this month. Can you generate a quality metrics report?
Hello BrachyBot. I am a new user and I accidentally uploaded the wrong CT scan. How do I clear the current data and start over with the correct patient scan?
Hi. I work in a department that primarily uses cobalt-60 for HDR brachytherapy instead of iridium-192. Can this system handle Co-60 source data for dose calculations?
Good morning. I am preparing for a board certification exam in radiation oncology. Can you help me review brachytherapy concepts and quiz me on treatment planning principles?
Hello. Before I begin, I want to make sure I understand the scope of this tool. Is BrachyBot intended to replace the physicist's judgment, or is it a decision-support tool? What are the limitations?

I have uploaded a CT scan for a prostate cancer patient. The scan was acquired with 3mm slice thickness and includes the pelvis from the iliac crests to the ischial tuberosities. Please analyze the image quality, identify the prostate gland, and assess whether the scan quality is sufficient for brachytherapy planning.

This CT scan shows a patient with cervical cancer. I need you to evaluate the tumor extent visible on CT, identify the tandem and ovoid applicator that was placed under anesthesia, and assess the applicator position relative to the cervix and uterus. Please provide measurements of the applicator geometry.

I uploaded a CT scan of a patient scheduled for prostate seed implant. The scan was done in the lithotomy position with a ultrasound probe in place. Please identify the prostate, seminal vesicles, bladder, and rectum, and provide approximate volumes for each structure.

Please analyze this head and neck CT scan for a patient with oral tongue carcinoma. I need to assess the extent of the primary tumor, evaluate lymph node involvement, and determine if there is mandibular invasion visible on CT.

This is a chest CT scan for a patient with endobronchial tumor who may be a candidate for endoluminal brachytherapy. Please evaluate the tumor location, degree of luminal obstruction, proximity to the carina, and identify any atelectasis or post-obstructive changes.

I have uploaded a post-implant CT scan for a prostate brachytherapy patient. The scan was taken 30 days after I-125 seed implantation. Please analyze the seed distribution, identify any seed migration to the lungs, and provide an assessment of overall implant quality.

Please examine this CT scan of a rectal cancer patient. The patient has a T3N1 rectal adenocarcinoma located 5cm from the anal verge. Assess the relationship of the tumor to the mesorectal fascia, evaluate for extramural vascular invasion, and determine the distance from the tumor to the anal sphincter.

This CT scan shows a breast cancer patient being considered for APBI. The lumpectomy cavity is visible in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast. Please identify the cavity, measure its dimensions, assess the chest wall distance, and evaluate the skin-to-cavity distance for balloon placement feasibility.

I have a CT scan for a patient with recurrent endometrial cancer at the vaginal cuff. The CT shows some soft tissue thickening at the cuff. Please analyze the extent of the recurrence, evaluate the relationship to the bladder and rectum, and assess whether brachytherapy is feasible.

Please analyze this CT scan for a patient with a penile cancer. The scan shows an exophytic lesion on the glans penis. Evaluate the depth of invasion, assess for inguinal lymph node involvement, and determine if the tumor is amenable to organ-preserving brachytherapy.

This CT scan is from a patient with biliary tract cancer. I need to evaluate the tumor extent along the bile duct, assess vascular involvement of the portal vein and hepatic artery, and determine if interstitial brachytherapy can be safely performed.

I have uploaded a CT scan for a patient with a vulvar melanoma. The primary lesion is on the right labium majus. Please evaluate the tumor dimensions, depth of invasion, assess for groin lymph node metastases, and determine if interstitial brachytherapy is appropriate for this patient.

Please analyze this CT scan of a pediatric patient with a bladder rhabdomyosarcoma. The patient is 4 years old. Evaluate the tumor extent, assess bladder wall invasion, evaluate for hydronephrosis, and determine if brachytherapy boost is indicated alongside external beam.

This CT scan shows a patient with advanced cervical cancer being evaluated for brachytherapy. There is a large cervical mass with parametrial extension. Please assess the tumor volume, evaluate the relationship to the pelvic sidewall, and measure the distance to the ureters.

I have uploaded a CT scan for a prostate cancer patient with a large prostate volume of approximately 80cc. Evaluate the prostate size, assess for median lobe protrusion into the bladder, and discuss whether this patient is suitable for brachytherapy or if neoadjuvant hormonal therapy should be considered.

Please analyze this CT scan of a patient with a skin cancer on the nose. The lesion is a 2cm squamous cell carcinoma. Evaluate the depth of invasion on CT, assess cartilage involvement, and determine if surface brachytherapy with a custom mold is feasible.

This CT scan is for a patient with esophageal cancer at the gastroesophageal junction. Evaluate the tumor length, assess the degree of luminal narrowing, evaluate for mediastinal lymphadenopathy, and determine if endoluminal brachytherapy boost is appropriate.

I uploaded a CT scan showing a patient with liver metastases from colorectal cancer. There are two lesions in the right hepatic lobe. Please segment the lesions, measure their volumes and positions relative to the hepatic vasculature, and assess whether image-guided brachytherapy is feasible.

Please analyze this CT scan for a patient with an anal canal cancer. The tumor is located at the dentate line. Evaluate the tumor extent, assess involvement of the internal and external sphincters, and determine if brachytherapy boost is indicated after external beam radiation.

This CT scan shows a patient with head and neck cancer requiring interstitial brachytherapy. There is a recurrent tumor in the floor of mouth. Please evaluate the tumor dimensions, assess mandibular proximity, evaluate the sublingual gland position, and determine optimal needle placement zones.

I have a CT scan for a female patient with a vaginal melanoma. The tumor is in the upper third of the vagina. Please evaluate the tumor extent, assess the relationship to the bladder and rectum, evaluate for lymph node involvement in the pelvis, and determine brachytherapy feasibility.

This is a post-implant CT scan taken at day 1 for a prostate brachytherapy patient. Please analyze the seed positions, evaluate edema by comparing with the pre-implant prostate volume, and provide an edema-corrected dosimetric assessment.

Please analyze this CT scan for a patient with a recurrent tumor at the anastomosis after rectal cancer surgery. The recurrence is at the colorectal anastomosis. Evaluate the tumor volume, assess invasion into surrounding pelvic structures, and determine if interstitial brachytherapy can be safely delivered.

This CT scan is for a patient with a urethral cancer. Please evaluate the tumor extent along the urethra, assess bladder involvement, evaluate for pelvic lymph node metastases, and determine if brachytherapy is appropriate for this rare malignancy.

I have uploaded a CT scan for quality assurance purposes. This is a CTCAE phantom scan with known dimensions. Please verify the geometric accuracy of the CT by measuring the phantom dimensions and comparing them to the known specifications to validate spatial calibration.

I am evaluating PET-CT for brachytherapy planning in cervical cancer. FDG-PET can visualize the primary tumor and lymph nodes. How should I integrate PET findings into brachytherapy target volume delineation? What are the limitations of PET for brachytherapy planning? How does PET-CT compare with MRI for target delineation? Should I use PET-CT routinely for brachytherapy planning?

I am performing a quality assurance check on the CT simulation for brachytherapy planning. I need to verify: (1) CT number accuracy using a phantom, (2) geometric accuracy of the CT images, (3) the effect of contrast material on CT-based dose calculation, and (4) the appropriate CT-to-electron-density conversion table for brachytherapy applicators. How do I perform each of these QA checks?

I need to understand how cone-beam CT (CBCT) can be used for brachytherapy guidance. What are the advantages of CBCT over conventional CT for brachytherapy? How does CBCT image quality compare to CT for applicator and target visualization? What are the radiation dose implications of using CBCT for brachytherapy guidance? Should I use CBCT routinely for brachytherapy fraction imaging?

I am evaluating the use of MRI for post-implant dosimetry evaluation of prostate LDR brachytherapy. How does MRI improve seed visualization compared to CT? What MRI sequences are best for seed localization? How does MRI-based post-implant dosimetry compare with CT-based evaluation? What are the practical challenges of MRI-based post-implant dosimetry?

I need to understand how to handle MRI artifacts in brachytherapy planning. What types of MRI artifacts can affect brachytherapy planning (susceptibility artifacts from metallic applicators, chemical shift artifacts, motion artifacts)? How do these artifacts affect target and applicator delineation? What correction methods exist? How should I adjust the MRI protocol to minimize artifacts?

I am evaluating the use of artificial intelligence (AI) for brachytherapy planning. How can AI assist in: (1) automatic applicator reconstruction from CT/MRI, (2) automatic target volume delineation, (3) dose optimization, and (4) plan quality evaluation? What are the current limitations of AI in brachytherapy? What validation studies exist for AI-based brachytherapy planning?

I am evaluating the use of MRI for brachytherapy planning in rectal cancer. How does MRI help in delineating the rectal tumor and mesorectal fascia? What MRI sequences are recommended for rectal cancer brachytherapy? How does MRI-based planning compare with CT-based planning for rectal brachytherapy? What are the challenges of MRI-guided rectal brachytherapy?

I am evaluating the accuracy of 3D ultrasound for brachytherapy guidance in gynecologic cancer. How does 3D ultrasound compare with MRI for target delineation? What are the advantages of 3D ultrasound over 2D ultrasound? Can 3D ultrasound replace MRI for brachytherapy planning in resource-limited settings? What are the training requirements for 3D ultrasound-guided brachytherapy?

I need to understand the role of artificial intelligence in automatic organ-at-risk delineation for brachytherapy. How accurate are current AI algorithms for OAR segmentation in the pelvis? What are the clinical requirements for AI-based OAR delineation? How should I validate AI-generated contours before using them in brachytherapy planning? What are the current limitations?

I am evaluating the use of spectral CT for brachytherapy planning. How does spectral CT improve material characterization compared to conventional CT? Can spectral CT reduce artifacts from brachytherapy applicators? What are the advantages for dose calculation? What are the current limitations?

I am evaluating the use of emerging imaging technologies for brachytherapy guidance. Are there any novel imaging modalities that could improve brachytherapy planning? What are the current research directions in brachytherapy imaging? How might photoacoustic imaging or optical coherence tomography be applied to brachytherapy? What is the timeline for clinical implementation?

Please segment the clinical target volume (CTV) for a prostate cancer brachytherapy case. The CT scan shows the prostate with the following characteristics: the prostate volume is approximately 35cc, there is no extraprostatic extension visible, and the patient has intermediate-risk disease with Gleason 3+4. Include the entire prostate gland with a minimal margin for microscopic disease.

I need you to segment the HR-CTV for a cervical cancer patient receiving HDR brachytherapy with tandem and ovoids. The MRI shows a 4cm cervical tumor with 1cm parametrial extension on the right side. The applicator is in good position. Please delineate the high-risk clinical target volume including the entire cervix and any visible residual tumor.

Please segment the clinical target volume for an endometrial cancer patient receiving vaginal cuff brachytherapy. The patient had a total hysterectomy for Stage IB endometrial cancer. The vaginal cuff is visible on CT with no residual disease. Define the treatment volume for the vaginal cuff boost.

I have a CT scan for a patient with anal cancer receiving chemoradiation followed by brachytherapy boost. The tumor is a 3cm lesion at the anal canal. Please segment the gross tumor volume (GTV) and clinical target volume (CTV) for the brachytherapy boost portion of treatment.

Please segment the CTV for a patient with a recurrent head and neck cancer in the oral tongue. The CT shows a 2.5cm recurrent squamous cell carcinoma in the left lateral tongue. Define the clinical target volume for interstitial brachytherapy, including the visible tumor and appropriate margins for microscopic spread.

For a breast cancer patient undergoing APBI with MammoSite, please segment the lumpectomy cavity and the planning target volume (PTV). The CT shows the lumpectomy cavity in the upper outer quadrant of the left breast with no surgical clips visible. Define appropriate margins for the PTV.

I need to segment the CTV for a patient with vaginal cancer. The tumor involves the upper third of the vagina, extending from the vaginal cuff to approximately 4cm distally. Please delineate the GTV and CTV for HDR brachytherapy, including the visible tumor and adjacent vaginal mucosa.

Please segment the prostate CTV for a patient with high-risk prostate cancer (Gleason 8, PSA 22, Stage T3a). The CT shows possible extraprostatic extension on the left side. Include the entire prostate and the region of suspected EPE with appropriate margins.

I have a CT scan for a patient with gallbladder cancer. The tumor is unresectable and interstitial brachytherapy is planned. Please segment the GTV encompassing the visible gallbladder tumor and define the CTV with appropriate margins considering the adjacent liver parenchyma and duodenum.

For a patient with rectal cancer at 3cm from the anal verge, please segment the CTV for brachytherapy boost after external beam chemoradiation. Include the tumor bed, mesorectal region, and perirectal lymph node stations in the CTV definition.

Please segment the HR-CTV and IR-CTV for a cervical cancer case with a larger tumor. The MRI shows a 6cm cervical tumor with bilateral parametrial invasion extending to the pelvic sidewall on the right. The tandem and ovoids are in place. Define both high-risk and intermediate-risk target volumes.

I need to segment the treatment volume for a patient with penile cancer. The tumor is on the glans penis, approximately 2cm in diameter, with suspected invasion into the corpus spongiosum. Please define the GTV and CTV for interstitial brachytherapy.

Please segment the target volume for a patient with nasopharyngeal carcinoma receiving intracavitary brachytherapy boost. The post-EBRT CT shows residual mucosal disease in the nasopharynx. Define the CTV for the brachytherapy boost.

For a patient with a skin cancer on the scalp, please segment the GTV and treatment volume for surface brachytherapy. The lesion is a 3cm basal cell carcinoma with irregular borders. The CT shows no deep invasion. Define the appropriate treatment volume.

I have a CT scan for a patient with urethral cancer involving the bulbar urethra. Please segment the GTV and CTV for HDR brachytherapy. The tumor extends approximately 3cm along the urethra. Define the treatment volumes for interstitial brachytherapy.

Please segment the CTV for a patient with an anal margin cancer. The tumor is a 4cm lesion at the anal margin extending into the perianal skin. For the brachytherapy boost, define the target volume including the visible tumor and a 1cm margin.

For a pancreatic cancer patient receiving intraoperative brachytherapy, please segment the tumor bed CTV. The patient had a partial resection with positive margins at the portal vein confluence. Define the CTV for the intraoperative HDR boost.

I need to segment the treatment volume for a patient with vulvar cancer. The primary tumor is on the left labium majus with a 3cm lesion. There is also a separate satellite lesion on the right labium minus. Define the GTV and CTV for interstitial brachytherapy covering both lesions.

Please segment the CTV for a patient with a urethral recurrence after radical prostatectomy. The CT shows soft tissue at the vesicourethral anastomosis. Define the target volume for salvage HDR brachytherapy including the anastomotic recurrence with appropriate margins.

For a patient with bile duct cancer, I need to segment the GTV and CTV for interstitial brachytherapy. The CT shows a tumor at the hilum of the liver involving the left and right hepatic ducts. Define the target volume considering the tumor extension along the bile ducts.

Please segment the HR-CTV for a cervical cancer patient treated with MRI-guided brachytherapy. The MRI shows a 3cm residual tumor after 45Gy external beam. The tandem and ring applicator is in place. Define the high-risk CTV based on MRI findings.

I have a CT scan for a patient with a parotid gland malignancy. The patient had a superficial parotidectomy and has a positive superficial margin. Please segment the surgical bed CTV for HDR brachytherapy boost with a 1cm margin.

For a patient with a recurrent tumor at the bronchial anastomosis after sleeve resection, please segment the GTV and CTV for endoluminal brachytherapy. The CT shows a 1.5cm nodule at the anastomosis site. Define the target volume for the endoluminal treatment.

Please segment the CTV for a patient with a pediatric pelvic rhabdomyosarcoma. The patient is 6 years old with a bladder neck tumor. After chemotherapy, there is a residual 2cm mass. Define the brachytherapy boost target volume considering the small pelvic anatomy.

I need to segment the target volumes for a patient with advanced cervical cancer undergoing MRI-guided adaptive brachytherapy. The pre-treatment MRI shows a 7cm tumor with bladder wall invasion and bilateral parametrial extension. Please segment the pre-treatment GTV, HR-CTV, and IR-CTV.

Please segment the organs at risk for a prostate brachytherapy case. The CT scan shows the pelvis with the prostate, bladder, rectum, and femoral heads clearly visible. Segment the bladder, rectum from the rectosigmoid junction to the anal verge, bilateral femoral heads, and the penile bulb.

For this cervical cancer brachytherapy case, please segment the critical OARs including the bladder (entire organ), rectum from peritoneal reflection to anal verge, sigmoid colon, and small bowel loops in the pelvis. The tandem and ovoids applicator is in place.

Please segment the OARs for a head and neck interstitial brachytherapy case. The patient has a floor of mouth tumor. Segment the mandible, bilateral parotid glands, spinal cord, brainstem, and the contralateral submandibular gland.

I need OAR segmentation for a breast APBI case using MammoSite. The CT shows the left breast with the lumpectomy cavity. Please segment the heart, bilateral lungs, contralateral breast, skin surface, and ribs on the treated side.

For this rectal cancer brachytherapy boost case, please segment the OARs. The tumor is at 5cm from the anal verge. Segment the bladder, reproductive organs (prostate in this male patient), bilateral femoral heads, and the small bowel loops within the pelvis.

Please segment the OARs for a patient receiving endoluminal brachytherapy for esophageal cancer. The CT covers the thorax. Segment the spinal cord, lungs, heart, trachea, and left main bronchus. Pay attention to the proximity of the tumor to these structures.

For a penile cancer interstitial brachytherapy case, please segment the OARs. The tumor is on the glans. Segment the urethra along its entire penile and bulbar course, the testes, and the anal sphincter complex. These structures must be carefully spared.

Please segment the OARs for a gallbladder interstitial brachytherapy case. The CT shows the upper abdomen. Segment the liver (uninvolved portion), duodenum, stomach, right kidney, and the spinal cord. The tumor is adjacent to the hepatic hilum.

For this anal cancer case receiving brachytherapy boost, please segment the OARs including the bladder, femoral heads, external anal sphincter, internal anal sphincter, and the vulva/perineal skin. The tumor is at the dentate line.

I need OAR segmentation for a nasopharyngeal carcinoma intracavitary brachytherapy case. Please segment the brainstem, spinal cord, bilateral temporal lobes, bilateral parotid glands, optic nerves, and the pituitary gland.

Please segment the OARs for a vaginal cancer brachytherapy case. The tumor is in the upper vagina. Segment the bladder, rectum, sigmoid colon, and bilateral ureters from the renal pelvis to the bladder insertion.

For a skin cancer on the nose receiving surface brachytherapy, please segment the critical structures. The lesion is on the nasal dorsum. Segment the eyeballs (bilateral), optic nerves, lens (bilateral), and the nasal cartilage framework.

Please segment the OARs for a liver metastases interstitial brachytherapy case. The CT shows two lesions in the right hepatic lobe. Segment the remaining liver parenchyma, hepatic vasculature (portal vein, hepatic veins, IVC), and both kidneys.

For a pediatric bladder rhabdomyosarcoma case, please segment the OARs in the small pelvis. The patient is 5 years old. Segment the bladder (if preserved), rectum, bilateral hip joints, and the growth plates of the proximal femurs.

Please segment the OARs for a patient with biliary tract cancer receiving interstitial brachytherapy. The tumor is at the pancreatic head. Segment the duodenum (C-loop), stomach, right kidney, spinal cord, and the portal vein.

For a vulvar cancer interstitial brachytherapy case, please segment the OARs. The tumor is on the left labium majus. Segment the urethra, vaginal canal, rectum, anus, and bilateral inguinal regions to define dose limits for lymph node sparing.

Please segment the OARs for a urethral cancer case receiving HDR interstitial brachytherapy. The tumor involves the bulbar urethra. Segment the bladder, rectum, anal sphincter, and the penile shaft distal to the tumor for dose assessment.

For an endometrial cancer case receiving vaginal cuff brachytherapy, please segment the OARs. The patient is post-hysterectomy. Segment the bladder, rectum, sigmoid colon, and the small bowel loops adjacent to the vaginal cuff.

Please segment the OARs for a patient with head and neck cancer receiving interstitial brachytherapy of the buccal mucosa. The tumor is in the right cheek. Segment the parotid glands (bilateral), mandible, spinal cord, and the muscles of mastication on the left side.

For a prostate brachytherapy case with a hip replacement artifact, please segment the OARs while accounting for the metal artifact. The left hip has a total hip replacement causing significant streak artifact. Segment the bladder, rectum, and note how the artifact may affect dose calculation.

Please segment the OARs for a case of anal canal cancer receiving concurrent chemoradiation with brachytherapy boost. The patient has a colostomy. The tumor is at 2cm from the anal verge. Segment the bladder, reproductive organs, and the colostomy stoma for dose assessment.

For a cervical cancer brachytherapy case, please segment the pelvic bones for dose evaluation. The patient has a tandem and ring applicator. Segment the sacrum, bilateral iliac bones, bilateral ischium, and bilateral acetabula to evaluate bone dose.

Please segment the OARs for a patient with an ocular melanoma receiving plaque brachytherapy. The CT shows the orbit with the globe. Segment the optic nerve, lens, lacrimal gland, and the contralateral eye for dose comparison.

For a head and neck cancer interstitial brachytherapy case, please segment the major blood vessels. The tumor is at the base of tongue. Segment the internal carotid arteries (bilateral), external carotid arteries, and the jugular veins to ensure safe dose delivery.

Please segment the OARs for a patient with a large prostate (80cc) for LDR brachytherapy planning. The CT shows significant prostatic calcifications. Segment the bladder, rectum, urethra (identified by Foley catheter), and bilateral obturator internus muscles.

I need help planning an LDR prostate brachytherapy case using I-125 seeds. The patient is 65 years old with intermediate-risk prostate cancer (Gleason 3+4, PSA 9.8, T2a). The prostate volume is 32cc. Please create a preplan with appropriate seed loading, including peripheral loading pattern with a minimum of 100 seeds. The prescription dose should be 145 Gy.

For a cervical cancer patient, I need an HDR brachytherapy plan using tandem and ovoids applicator. The tandem length is 6cm, ovoid diameter is 2.5cm. The prescription dose is 5.5 Gy per fraction to point A, delivered in 5 fractions with 2 fractions per day. Please optimize the dwell positions and dwell times to maximize target coverage while respecting OAR constraints.

Please plan a breast APBI treatment using a MammoSite balloon catheter. The balloon-to-skin distance is 7mm, and the balloon volume is 42cc. The prescription dose is 34 Gy in 10 fractions. I need the dwell positions optimized to provide adequate dose coverage of the PTV while minimizing skin dose.

I have an endometrial cancer patient who needs vaginal cuff brachytherapy. The patient is post-hysterectomy. Using a vaginal cylinder applicator with 2.5cm diameter, please plan the HDR treatment with a prescription dose of 3 Gy per fraction to 0.5cm depth, delivered in 5 fractions for adjuvant treatment.

For a prostate cancer patient with a large prostate of 75cc, I need help with neoadjuvant hormonal therapy planning followed by brachytherapy. After 3 months of LHRH agonist, the prostate has shrunk to 52cc. Please create an LDR plan using Pd-103 seeds with a prescription dose of 100 Gy.

Please create an HDR brachytherapy plan for an anal cancer boost. The patient has a 3cm anal canal tumor and has received 45Gy in 25 fractions of external beam. The boost plan should use a single-channel rectal applicator with 3 fractions of 5 Gy each. Optimize dwell positions to cover the tumor while sparing the bladder and rectum.

I need an HDR plan for a patient with oral tongue cancer receiving interstitial brachytherapy. The implant has 8 needles placed 1cm apart in a single plane. The active length of each needle is 4cm. The prescription dose is 6 Gy per fraction in 3 fractions. Please optimize the dwell positions to achieve a uniform dose distribution across the implant.

For a patient with recurrent endometrial cancer at the vaginal cuff, I need a PDR brachytherapy plan. The prescription dose is equivalent to 60 Gy in 2 Gy fractions using LDR equivalent calculations. The pulse schedule should be 0.5 Gy per hour over 48 hours. Please create the plan using a vaginal cylinder with dwell positions.

Please plan an HDR prostate brachytherapy case using a template-guided approach. The patient has a 28cc prostate with a planned 18 needles. The prescription dose is 9 Gy per fraction in 2 fractions. Optimize the dwell positions across all needles to achieve D90 > 100% and V100 > 95% while keeping the urethral Dmax below 110% of the prescription dose.

I have a cervical cancer patient with a tandem and ring applicator. The tandem is 6cm with a 15-degree curvature. The ring diameter is 26mm. Please plan the HDR treatment with 4 fractions of 7 Gy each, delivered twice daily. The target is HR-CTV D90 > 87 Gy EQD2, and I need the D2cc of the bladder < 80 Gy EQD2 and rectum < 70 Gy EQD2.

For a head and neck cancer patient, please plan an interstitial brachytherapy boost using the Paris system. The implant consists of 6 parallel needles at 1.8cm spacing with an active length of 5cm. The prescription dose is 20 Gy delivered in 4 fractions. The treatment volume is a 3cm x 2.5cm x 2cm tumor in the buccal mucosa.

Please create a prostate brachytherapy preplan for a patient with a prior TURP. The prostate volume is 28cc with a TURP defect in the median lobe. The prescription dose is 145 Gy with I-125 seeds. I need the plan to account for the TURP defect by adjusting seed positions to avoid the defect region while maintaining adequate peripheral dose.

For a vulvar cancer patient, I need an HDR interstitial brachytherapy plan. The template has 10 needles placed in a modified Paris configuration around a 4cm tumor on the left labium. The prescription dose is 4 Gy per fraction in 8 fractions. Optimize dwell times to achieve good target coverage while keeping the urethral and rectal doses within tolerance.

I need an HDR plan for endoluminal brachytherapy of a bronchial tumor. The patient has a 2cm endobronchial lesion in the right main bronchus. Using a 6 French catheter with 6 dwell positions, plan the treatment with 5 Gy per fraction in 3 fractions. The dose should be prescribed at 1cm from the source axis.

For a gallbladder cancer case, please plan an interstitial HDR brachytherapy treatment. The GTV is approximately 4cm x 3cm x 3cm adjacent to the liver hilum. I plan to place 6 needles through the percutaneous approach. The prescription dose is 6 Gy per fraction in 3 fractions. Optimize dwell positions to cover the GTV while limiting the duodenal D2cc.

Please create a surface brachytherapy plan for a skin cancer on the chest wall. The lesion is 3cm x 2cm, and I am using a custom surface applicator with 4 dwell positions. The prescription dose is 4 Gy per fraction in 8 fractions to 5mm depth. Optimize to provide uniform dose across the treatment area while limiting dose to the underlying lung.

I have a patient with a large rectal tumor (5cm from anal verge, T3N1) who has completed 45Gy EBRT. I need a brachytherapy boost plan using HDR. Place 8 interstitial needles through a transperineal approach around the tumor. Plan with 3 fractions of 5 Gy each. Optimize to cover the tumor while respecting the prostate and bladder dose constraints.

For a patient with urethral cancer, please plan an HDR interstitial brachytherapy treatment. The tumor involves 4cm of the bulbar urethra. Using a template with 8 needles, plan 4 fractions of 4.5 Gy each. The urethra must be at the center of the implant, and the plan must limit the rectal D2cc while maintaining target coverage.

I need a combined EBRT plus brachytherapy plan for a patient with locally advanced cervical cancer. The patient will receive 45Gy in 25 fractions to the pelvis followed by HDR brachytherapy. Using a tandem and ovoids applicator, plan 4 fractions of 7 Gy each to point A. Calculate the total EQD2 to point A and the relevant OARs.

For a prostate cancer patient with bilateral hip replacements causing artifact, plan an LDR I-125 seed implant. The prostate volume is 38cc. Due to the artifact, CT-based dose calculation may be inaccurate. Please plan using modified seed positions that avoid the regions with severe artifact and discuss the limitations of the plan.

Please plan an HDR brachytherapy treatment for a patient with nasopharyngeal carcinoma. The patient has residual mucosal disease after 70Gy EBRT. Using an intracavitary applicator, plan 3 fractions of 5 Gy each. The dose must cover the nasopharyngeal mucosa while sparing the brainstem (D2cc < 60 Gy EQD2) and temporal lobes.

Complete physics of brachytherapy source calibration: RAKR definition, well chamber methodology, traceability chain (NIST/NPL), source decay characteristics (Ir-192, Co-60, Cs-137), verification procedures, and regulatory documentation.

Complete TPS commissioning for brachytherapy: acceptance testing, TG-59 tests, source data verification, dose calculation algorithm validation, source exchange commissioning, imaging protocol optimization, and ongoing QA.

Dose optimization in brachytherapy: forward vs inverse planning, optimization algorithms (gradient, simulated annealing, genetic), dwell time optimization, constrained vs unconstrained, objectives/constraints, clinical trade-offs, and ML in optimization.

Tandem and ovoid applicator system: historical development, anatomical basis, mechanical principles, dosimetric characteristics, applicator selection criteria, loading patterns (Manchester vs modern), and ring vs ovoid design comparison.

Image-guided adaptive brachytherapy for cervical cancer: adaptive definition, MRI protocol, target delineation on MRI, dose optimization per fraction, cumulative dose reporting methodology, and clinical outcomes vs conventional 2D.

Pulse-dose-rate brachytherapy: physical delivery method, radiobiological rationale, equivalence to LDR/HDR (incomplete repair model), clinical applications, technical advantages, dosimetric considerations, and clinical evidence.

Brachytherapy for head and neck cancer: historical role in oral cavity, interstitial technique, dose/fractionation, OAR relationships (mandible, salivary glands), functional outcomes, current role vs IMRT/TORS, and remaining indications.

DVH analysis in brachytherapy: cumulative vs differential DVH construction, statistical parameters, limitations as 2D representation, combined analysis with spatial maps, DSH for hollow organs, and GEC-ESTRO/EMBRACE reporting requirements.

Brachytherapy source security and transportation: NRC/state regulations, transportation procedures, storage requirements (vault design), chain of custody, source tracking systems, emergency procedures for loss/theft, training requirements, and violation penalties.

Applicator reconstruction in treatment planning: 2D point-based vs 3D CT vs MRI methods, imaging protocols, challenges (artifacts), software tools, verification procedures, impact on dose calculation, and QA procedures.

Tumor hypoxia and brachytherapy implications: mechanisms (perfusion vs diffusion-limited), OER value, oxygen fixation hypothesis, clinical evidence in gynecologic cancers, hypoxia assessment methods, strategies to overcome, and brachytherapy's dose escalation advantage.

Radiation-induced second malignancies after brachytherapy: risk estimates, latency periods, dose-response models (LNT vs threshold), site-specific risks, dose gradient advantage vs EBRT, chemotherapy additive risk, and surveillance recommendations.

Tumor control probability model in brachytherapy: Poisson formulation, parameter effects (cell density, radiosensitivity), dose heterogeneity impact, EUD concept, clinical validation (EMBRACE dose-response), limitations, and optimization application.

Normal tissue complication probability model in brachytherapy: LKB formulation, organ parameters (TD50, m, n), volume effect for serial/parallel organs, DVH reduction rationale, EMBRACE validation, limitations, and multi-criteria optimization application.

Plan quality metrics in brachytherapy: COIN definition/interpretation, homogeneity index, conformity index, coverage index, limitations of single metrics, clinical applications, and Pareto-optimal multi-objective evaluation.

Pediatric brachytherapy: unique considerations (growth, second malignancy), common tumor sites (vaginal RMS, ependymoma, retinoblastoma), applicator design challenges, developing organ dose constraints, anesthesia requirements, psychosocial impact, and long-term follow-up.

Radiation safety in brachytherapy: ALARA principle, time-distance-shielding, regulatory dose limits, HDR room design (interlocks, monitoring), permanent seed precautions, waste management, and emergency procedures (stuck source, contamination).

Quality of life impact of cervical cancer brachytherapy: validated instruments (EORTC QLQ-CX24, FACT-Cx), affected domains, acute/long-term outcomes, sexual function impact, technique comparison (2D vs IGABT), interventions (dilation, rehabilitation), and decision-making integration.

Brachytherapy for vulvar cancer: primary and adjuvant indications, applicator selection (interstitial, surface), target volume definition, dose/fractionation, OAR constraints (urethra, clitoris, femoral vessels), wound healing considerations, functional outcomes, and published evidence.

Brachytherapy for esophageal cancer: historical role, indications (definitive, palliative, neoadjuvant), applicator selection, dose/fractionation, OAR constraints (trachea, aorta, spinal cord), complications (fistula, perforation), trial evidence, and current role.

48yo M, recurrent HPV- oropharyngeal cancer (2cm surgical bed) after IMRT 70Gy + TORS 2y ago. Severe dysphagia (MDADI 45/100), PEG-dependent, bilateral vocal cord paralysis. Salvage interstitial plan.

55yo F, recurrent IIB cervical cancer (1.5cm left parametrium) after CRT. Crohn's disease (infliximab, remission), severe aortic stenosis (valve area 0.8cm), bilateral LE lymphedema. Interstitial plan with multiple comorbidities.
48yo F with IIB cervical cancer (6cm), EBRT 45Gy + cisplatin. Tandem/ring + 4 interstitial needles. Fraction 2 completed. AKI: creatinine 0.9→2.1, oliguria. Emergency management plan.

72yo F, recurrent Grade 3 serous endometrial (2cm vaginal cuff) after hysterectomy + EBRT 45Gy 3y ago. Severe neuropathy (taxane, walking aid), bilateral LE edema, recurrent UTIs. Interstitial plan with functional limitations.

60yo M, 3cm T2N0M0 prostate (Gleason 4+3=7, PSA 12, 50cc). Combined EBRT 46Gy + HDR boost 18Gy/2fx. Total colectomy (end ileostomy), neurogenic bladder (CIC 4x daily), peripheral neuropathy. Absent rectum plan.

48yo F, IIB cervical cancer (5cm), EBRT 45Gy/carboplatin (cisplatin intolerance). Tandem/ovoid in place. Residual 2.5cm, left parametrial. CINV history, anxiety (sertraline), GERD (omeprazole). Supportive care challenges.

70yo M, recurrent Gleason 5+4=9 (T3bN0M0) after RP + salvage EBRT 64Gy 5y ago. Anastomotic mass 2cm extending to bladder neck. Bladder diverticulum 2.5cm, ureteral stricture disease. Salvage HDR plan.

38yo F, IIIC1 cervical cancer (4cm), EBRT 45Gy/cisplatin. Tandem/ovoid in place. Olympic track cyclist. Iron deficiency anemia, left tibial stress fracture (healed 6mo ago), OCP use. Athletic performance concerns.
65yo M, 3cm Gleason 4+5=9 prostate (T3a, PSA 25, 75cc). EBRT 50Gy + HDR boost 26Gy/2fx. Prior APR 10y ago (colostomy), right inguinal hernia mesh. Altered pelvic anatomy plan.

52yo F, 2.5cm recurrent Grade 3 serous endometrial at vaginal apex after hysterectomy + EBRT 45Gy 3y ago. New breast cancer (ER+ PR+ HER2-, 1.5cm, node-negative). Treatment sequencing for two cancers.

45yo M, 2cm T1N0M0 penile cancer (glans) after Fournier gangrene (3y ago, scarring). Type 1 DM (insulin pump, HbA1c 7.2%), smoking history. Penile-preserving brachytherapy with wound healing concerns.

60yo F, 3.5cm IIIC1 endometrial cancer (Grade 2 endometrioid). Post TAH-BSO + EBRT 45Gy/carbo. VBT planned. Post-gastric bypass (BMI 35, from 48), IDDM (HbA1c 8.5%), OSA (BiPAP). VBT with altered anatomy.

75yo M, recurrent Gleason 3+4=7 (PSA 6.5) after RP + salvage EBRT 66Gy 6y ago. Solitary anastomotic recurrence. ESRD (dialysis 3x/wk), CAD (2 MIs, EF 30%), bilateral BKA. Wheelchair user. Salvage HDR with severe functional limitations.
32yo F, IA2 cervical adenocarcinoma with LVSI (conization specimen), negative margins. Desires fertility preservation. Observation vs adjuvant VBT decision framework with competing risks.

58yo M, T1cN0M0 Gleason 3+4=7, PSA 10.5, 42cc. Permanent seed implant. Bilateral hip replacements, severe lumbar stenosis (epidural q3mo), bilateral carpal tunnel (post-decompression L). Positioning challenges.

45yo F, IIB cervical cancer (4cm). EBRT 45Gy/cisplatin. Tandem/ovoid + 4 needles. Fraction 1 delivered. TPS software error: dwell times based on incorrect source strength (actual 10% weaker). Immediate response.

58yo F, recurrent high-grade serous ovarian cancer (platinum-sensitive, 20mo relapse). 3.5cm vaginal + 1.5cm peritoneal deposit. Post-6x carbo/gem with response. Debulking + IP chemo + VBT boost. Prior bowel obstruction.

42yo M, 2cm T1N0M0 oral tongue SCC after partial glossectomy, 1mm positive margin. Adjuvant interstitial brachytherapy. Alcohol use disorder (sober 5y, naltrexone), HCV (SVR), nicotine dependence. Anxiety about speech/swallowing.

70yo F, recurrent IIIB cervical cancer (2.5cm central) after CRT. Pelvic exenteration + IORT. Severe aortic stenosis (valve area 0.6cm, NYHA III), severe osteoporosis (T-score -4.0, 3 vertebral fractures), rivaroxaban. Complex pre-operative plan.

55yo M, 2.5cm Gleason 3+4=7 (T2b, 42cc). Permanent seed implant. Crohn's (ileocolonic, adalimumab, remission), prior small bowel resection (20cm ileum), reversed loop ileostomy, bile acid malabsorption. Plan with IBD.

48yo F, 2.5cm Stage I vaginal SCC. Definitive interstitial brachytherapy. BMI 45, IDDM (insulin pump, HbA1c 9.0%), severe OSA (AHI 45, CPAP), bilateral LE lymphedema, chronic pain (gabapentin, duloxetine). Multiple comorbidities plan.

65yo M, 3cm T2N0M0 Gleason 4+3=7 (PSA 12, 50cc). EBRT 46Gy + HDR boost 18Gy/2fx. Total colectomy for UC (end ileostomy), neurogenic bladder (CIC 4x daily), peripheral neuropathy. HDR with absent rectum.
45yo F, IIB cervical cancer (5cm). EBRT 45Gy/cisplatin. Tandem/ovoid placed. Latex allergy (anaphylaxis). Standard applicator has latex components. Alternative approach and emergency preparedness.

70yo M, 3cm Gleason 4+3=7 (T3a, PSA 15, 65cc). EBRT 50Gy + HDR boost 26Gy/2fx. Metastatic colon cancer (liver resected 8y ago, disease-free), T1DM (insulin pump, HbA1c 7.5%), cardiac stent (aspirin + clopidogrel). Multiple cancer and comorbidity management.

52yo F, 2.5cm Stage I vaginal SCC (posterior wall). Definitive interstitial brachytherapy. Severe claustrophobia (no MRI), latex allergy (anaphylaxis), mechanical mitral valve (warfarin INR 2.5), CKD (GFR 42). Multiple medical constraints plan.

I am treating a 68-year-old male with prostate cancer (Gleason 4+5, Stage T3b, PSA 35, node-positive on PET-CT). He has a history of Crohn disease with an end colostomy, moderate COPD (FEV1 52%), and a mechanical aortic valve requiring lifelong warfarin (INR target 2.5-3.5). Current INR is 2.8. He had a DVT 2 years ago on a previous anticoagulation regimen. He wants definitive treatment. Given his extensive comorbidities, what treatment approach would you recommend? How do I manage his warfarin during brachytherapy? What concurrent chemotherapy should I add? What are the competing mortality risks?

I am treating a 60-year-old male with a 4 cm anal canal squamous cell carcinoma (Stage III, T3N1M0). He has well-controlled HIV with CD4 count of 420 and undetectable viral load on antiretroviral therapy. He has a history of IV drug use (clean for 5 years) and hepatitis C (SVR achieved). He has moderate depression requiring sertraline. He has no prior radiation. Standard treatment is concurrent chemoradiation (Nigro protocol). Should I modify the standard radiation dose or fractionation given his HIV status? Should I consider brachytherapy boost? What concurrent chemotherapy would be appropriate? How should I manage his depression during treatment?

I have a 72-year-old male with a 2 cm prostate cancer (Gleason 3+3, Stage T1c, PSA 6.0) who has end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis (3 times weekly). He has a well-functioning arteriovenous fistula in his left arm. He has a history of renal cell carcinoma treated with right nephrectomy 10 years ago. He is on warfarin for atrial fibrillation (target INR 2.0-3.0, current INR 2.4). He wants definitive treatment. Given his ESRD, warfarin use, and solitary kidney history, should I recommend LDR brachytherapy? How do I manage his warfarin and dialysis schedule around the procedure? What dose modifications are needed?

I have a 60-year-old female with a 4 cm endometrial cancer (Grade 3, Stage IB) who is a professional opera singer. She had a total hysterectomy with BSO and pelvic lymphadenectomy (negative nodes). She needs adjuvant therapy. She is very concerned about vaginal stenosis and its impact on her singing career (she uses her pelvic floor extensively for singing technique). She wants to minimize treatment-related side effects. Should I recommend vaginal cuff brachytherapy alone or combined EBRT and brachytherapy? What fractionation would minimize vaginal side effects? What vaginal dilation protocol should I recommend?

I am treating a 50-year-old female with a 4 cm vulvar cancer (squamous cell, Stage II, depth of invasion 5 mm, 2 mm margins after radical vulvectomy). She has a positive left inguinal sentinel lymph node (0.3 mm deposit). She has a history of morbid obesity (BMI 48, lost 30 kg with bariatric surgery 2 years ago, current BMI 35). She has residual redundant skin in the inguinal region. She has well-controlled type 2 diabetes (HbA1c 7.0%). She needs adjuvant therapy. Should I recommend adjuvant radiation to the vulvar bed and inguinal regions? What brachytherapy approach could address the vulvar bed? How does her body habitus affect radiation planning?

I have a 70-year-old female with a 2 cm endometrial cancer (Grade 1, Stage IA) who has severe aortic stenosis (valve area 0.7 cm2, peak gradient 58 mmHg). She is not a surgical candidate due to her cardiac risk. Her cardiologist says she has a 5-year survival of approximately 40% from her cardiac disease. She wants definitive treatment. Should I recommend definitive brachytherapy alone? What fractionation would minimize treatment visits? What anesthesia considerations are important? Should I consider active surveillance given her limited cardiac life expectancy?

I am managing a 32-year-old female with a recurrent cervical cancer (Stage IIIB) after radical hysterectomy and adjuvant chemoradiation (50.4 Gy EBRT + cisplatin + 30 Gy brachytherapy boost completed 10 months ago). The recurrence is a 4 cm central pelvic mass with bladder invasion causing hematuria. She has bilateral hydronephrosis requiring nephrostomy tubes. Her performance status is ECOG 2. Her creatinine is 2.8 (baseline 0.8). She has lost 15 kg in the past 3 months. Given the extensive prior radiation, poor performance status, and renal impairment, should I recommend re-irradiation, systemic therapy, or best supportive care? What systemic options exist?

I am treating a 45-year-old female with a 3 cm breast cancer (Stage I, triple negative, BRCA1 positive) who had a lumpectomy with close margins (1 mm). She is very physically active and a competitive swimmer. She wants breast-conserving therapy and refuses re-excision. She is concerned about long-term radiation effects on her swimming performance. She asks about the comparison between whole breast radiation, accelerated partial breast irradiation with brachytherapy, and proton therapy. She wants the treatment with the fewest side effects and shortest treatment duration. Given her triple negative histology and BRCA status, which approach would you recommend?

I am managing a 48-year-old male with a 5 cm prostate cancer (Gleason 4+4, Stage T3a, PSA 22) who has a history of severe opioid use disorder (in sustained remission for 3 years on buprenorphine/naloxone). He has chronic pain from degenerative disc disease requiring ongoing opioid management. He has well-controlled hepatitis C from his prior IV drug use (SVR achieved). He has depression treated with venlafaxine. He wants definitive treatment. Given his substance abuse history and ongoing opioid use, should I recommend LDR brachytherapy? How does his buprenorphine/naloxone affect treatment? Should I adjust his pain management during brachytherapy? What are the implications for treatment compliance?

I uploaded a CT scan for patient John Smith earlier. Can you remind me what the prostate volume was on that scan? I remember it was around 35cc but I want to confirm the exact measurement from the segmentation.

Can you recall what dose prescription we agreed on for the prostate LDR case we reviewed this morning? I think we decided on 145 Gy with I-125 but I want to make sure we didn't change it later in the discussion.
Earlier you provided dosimetric parameters for the rectal cancer boost case. Can you remind me what the GTV D90 was and whether the rectal D2cc was within the tolerance limit?
We planned a nasal skin cancer case with surface brachytherapy. Can you recall the lesion dimensions, the applicator type we chose, and the dose prescription we agreed upon?

For a cervical cancer brachytherapy case, the tandem is placed at an angle of 60 degrees from the horizontal. If the tandem length is 6 cm and the source dwell positions are spaced at 5 mm intervals, calculate the expected dose rate at Point A (2 cm lateral and 2 cm superior from the tandem tip) using the TG-43 formalism for an Ir-192 source with an air-kerma strength of 40,000 uCi.

A brachytherapy source has an air-kerma strength of 38,500 uCi as measured on January 15. The source decay constant for Ir-192 is 0.00974 day^-1. Calculate the expected air-kerma strength on February 15 (31 days later) and determine the required treatment time to deliver 6 Gy at a reference point if the dose rate at that point on January 15 was 200 cGy/min.

A prostate HDR brachytherapy plan uses 16 catheters with a total of 96 dwell positions. The average dwell time is 8.5 seconds per position, and the source speed is 25 cm/sec. Calculate the total source travel time, the estimated treatment delivery time (excluding transit), and determine whether the treatment can be completed within a 45-minute appointment slot including setup and verification time.

For a vaginal cylinder brachytherapy treatment, the prescription is 5 Gy per fraction at a depth of 5 mm from the cylinder surface. The cylinder diameter is 2.5 cm. Using the TG-43 formalism for a line source, calculate the dwell time required at the central dwell position to achieve the prescribed dose. Assume an Ir-192 source with air-kerma strength of 35,000 uCi.

A brachytherapy plan requires the calculation of the equivalent dose in 2 Gy fractions (EQD2) for a cumulative rectal dose. The patient received 45 Gy in 25 fractions of external beam radiation (alpha/beta = 3 for rectum), followed by brachytherapy delivering 28 Gy in 4 fractions of 7 Gy each. Calculate the total EQD2 to the rectum, assuming the brachytherapy dose is delivered to D2cc.

A treatment plan uses a ring applicator with an inner diameter of 2.6 cm. The prescribed dose is delivered at the isodose surface that encompasses 100% of the applicator surface. If the dose at the applicator surface is 150% of the prescription dose, calculate the dose at 5 mm and 10 mm from the applicator surface using the point source approximation. Discuss the accuracy limitations of this approximation.

For a complex interstitial brachytherapy implant of the cervix using 8 needles with an average of 5 dwell positions each, calculate the total number of dwell time optimization parameters. If the optimizer uses a gradient-based algorithm with a convergence threshold of 0.1%, estimate the number of iterations required for convergence. How does this compare to a 5-needle configuration?

A brachytherapy source is calibrated to have an air-kerma strength of 40,000 uCi. The treatment is planned for 14 days after calibration. Using the AAPM TG-43 formalism, calculate the required correction factor for the changed source strength on the treatment day, and determine the adjusted treatment time if the planned time at calibration was 350 seconds.

For a patient with a tandem and ovoids applicator, the tandem angle is 70 degrees and the ovoid separation is 2 cm. Calculate the dose contribution from each dwell position in the tandem to the ICRU 38 bladder point (located 2 cm posterior and 2 cm superior from the tandem-ovoid junction). Present the calculation for a 6 cm tandem with 12 dwell positions at 5 mm intervals.

A center needs to verify the positional accuracy of its afterloader source stepping mechanism. The afterloader is programmed to place the source at positions 0, 10, 20, 30, 40, and 50 mm from a reference point. Using radiochromic film measurements, the actual source positions were measured as 0.2, 10.1, 19.8, 30.3, 39.9, and 50.1 mm. Evaluate these measurements against the TG-59 tolerance criteria and determine if the afterloader passes the positional accuracy test.

Calculate the volume of the high-risk clinical target volume (HR-CTV) for a cervical cancer patient based on the following MRI measurements: the tumor extends 3.5 cm craniocaudally, 4.2 cm transversely, and 3.8 cm anteroposteriorly. Using an ellipsoidal volume approximation, calculate the HR-CTV volume and compare it to the typical HR-CTV volumes reported in the EMBRACE studies. Is this volume consistent with a Stage IIB cervical cancer?

A brachytherapy plan uses geometric optimization with a reference point at the isocenter of the applicator. The plan has 8 dwell positions with equal initial dwell times of 10 seconds. After optimization, the dwell times range from 2.5 seconds to 18.7 seconds. Calculate the dwell time modulation ratio (maximum/minimum) and evaluate whether this modulation is clinically acceptable. What is the typical range of modulation ratios seen in clinical practice?

For a patient receiving pulsed-dose-rate (PDR) brachytherapy, the planned dose rate at the reference point is 0.5 Gy/hour with pulses delivered every hour. The prescribed dose is 30 Gy delivered over 60 hours. Calculate the dose per pulse, the total number of pulses, and determine the BED for tumor (alpha/beta = 10) and late-responding normal tissue (alpha/beta = 3).

A center is validating its treatment planning system dose calculation for a ring applicator. The TG-43 based calculation at 1 cm from the ring center gives 8.5 Gy/min. An independent calculation using a spreadsheet-based TG-43 algorithm gives 8.3 Gy/min. Calculate the percentage discrepancy between the two calculations and evaluate whether it falls within the TG-59 recommended tolerance of 5% for independent dose verification.

Calculate the dose rate constant (Lambda) corrected dose rate at 1 cm from an Ir-192 source with an air-kerma strength of 42,000 uCi. Use the TG-43 dose rate constant of 1.108 cGy/(hr*uCi) and the geometry function for a line source of length 3.5 mm at a distance of 1 cm. Show all steps of the calculation.

A brachytherapy center treats 200 patients per year with an average of 4 fractions per patient. Each fraction requires approximately 45 minutes of physicist time for plan review and treatment supervision. Calculate the annual physicist time commitment for brachytherapy, convert to FTE, and evaluate whether the center has adequate physicist staffing based on the AAPM TG-301 recommendation of 1 physicist FTE per 150 brachytherapy patients per year.

For a prostate HDR treatment using 18 catheters, each with 15 dwell positions spaced at 5 mm intervals, calculate the total number of potential source positions. If the treatment planning system optimizes dwell times for all positions, what is the total number of dwell time variables? If the source can be placed at any 1 mm increment instead of 5 mm, how does this affect the number of optimization variables?

A patient receives a vaginal cuff brachytherapy boost of 15 Gy in 5 fractions following 50 Gy of EBRT. The vaginal cylinder has a diameter of 2.5 cm and the prescribed depth is 5 mm. Calculate the D2cc to the rectum and sigmoid from the brachytherapy boost alone using published dose-volume data for similar cylinder sizes. Then calculate the cumulative EQD2 to these organs from both EBRT and brachytherapy.

Calculate the tissue attenuation correction factor for a brachytherapy source at a distance of 3 cm from a dwell position, assuming soft tissue with a linear attenuation coefficient of 0.105 cm^-1 for Ir-192 gamma rays. Compare this to the TG-43 water-based calculation which does not account for tissue heterogeneities. What is the percentage difference?

For an interstitial brachytherapy implant using the Paris system, the implant consists of 6 needles arranged in a triangular configuration with 1.5 cm spacing. The active length of each needle is 4 cm. Calculate the reference dose rate at the central axis of the implant and determine the treatment time required to deliver 30 Gy at the reference dose rate.
Calculate total EQD2 at point A for EBRT 45 Gy/25fx + HDR 7 Gy x4 (alpha/beta 10). Also calculate bladder D2cc EQD2 (EBRT 55 Gy + HDR 6.2 Gy x4, alpha/beta 3). Show all steps.
Calculate total air-kerma strength (90 seeds x 0.5 U), dose-rate at prescription point (Lambda=1.27 cGy/U/hr), and time to deliver 145 Gy. Discuss I-125 decay (t1/2=59.4 days).
Calculate BED and EQD2 for prostate (ab=1.5), urethra (ab=3), rectum (ab=3) with 38 Gy/4fx: D90=40, urethra Dmax=44, rectum D2cc=30. Show all calculation steps.
Calculate cumulative EQD2 for EBRT 50.4 Gy/28fx + HDR 30 Gy/5fx: point A tumor (ab=10), bladder D2cc (48 Gy EBRT + 6.5 Gy/fx HDR, ab=3), rectum D2cc (52 Gy EBRT + 5.8 Gy/fx HDR, ab=3).
Ir-192 RAKR verification: measured 4.85 at 45 days, initial 6.12. t1/2=73.83 days. Calculate expected RAKR, percentage discrepancy, and required actions.
Calculate dwell time for 3.5 Gy at 2 cm from Ir-192 source: Lambda=1.108, g(2)=0.985, F(2,pi/2)=1.0, SK=37,300 U. Show TG-43 steps.
Calculate total treatment time (sum of 4,250 sec dwell times), dose-rate at D90 point, and verify HDR classification (>12 Gy/hr).
Calculate PDR BED for 30 Gy/60 pulses (0.5 Gy/pulse, 1-hour interval, repair half-time 1.5 hr). Compare to equivalent HDR 38 Gy/4fx for late tissue.
Calculate dose at 1.5 cm from 3.5 cm Ir-192 line source using TG-43. Include geometry function for line source, dose-rate, and 5-minute delivery.
Calculate total air-kerma (80 x 0.85 U), initial dose-rate (Lambda=1.25), and time to 50% of 100 Gy prescription. Compare Pd-103 decay to I-125.
Verify TG-43: measured 125.4 cGy/hr vs planned 124.8 cGy/hr at 1 cm. Calculate percentage difference, evaluate TG-59 tolerance, and dose in 45 seconds.
Calculate cumulative EQD2 across EBRT 45 Gy + HDR 7 Gy x4 + VBT 5 Gy x3 for tumor, bladder, and rectum (ab=10 tumor, ab=3 OARs).
Calculate from nomogram: 85 seeds for 42 cc prostate, Rx=145 Gy, seed SK=0.42 U. Total air-kerma, estimated D90 (1.15 x Rx), and urethra D0.1cc at 120% Rx.
Calculate vaginal mucosa surface dose using inverse square law (surface at 0.1 cm vs Rx at 0.5 cm). Total over 3 fractions. Evaluate against mucosal tolerance.
Calculate average deviation, max deviation, and RMS from measured dwell positions (10 positions at 5 mm). Evaluate against TG-59 tolerance (1 mm).
Calculate Ir-192 source strength decay over 90 days from 8.5 Ci. Calculate Day 30/60/90 strengths, percentage decrease, treatment time changes, and replacement action level.
Calculate total treatment time from given tandem/ovoid dwell times. Calculate tandem/ovoid ratio and estimate transit time.
Independent TG-43 calculation: SK=38,500, Lambda=1.108, G=0.185, g=0.978, F=0.965. Calculate dose-rate and compare to TPS 85.3 cGy/hr.
Calculate femoral head dose (D2cc=8.5 Gy) as % of 145 Gy prescription. Calculate BED (ab=3) and EQD2. Compare to 50 Gy EQD2 fracture tolerance.
Calculate dose at point A from given dwell time distribution (tandem + ovoid). Verify HDR dose-rate classification.
Calculate PDR BED for 30 Gy/60 pulses (0.5 Gy, 1 hr intervals, t1/2=1.5 hr). Compare to continuous LDR 30 Gy/60 hr.
Calculate corrected air-kerma from well chamber: reading 12.85 nC, calibration 5.23x10^4 Gy/C, temp 22C, pressure 101.3 kPa, electrometer 1.003.
Calculate DGI (D2cc/D100) and HI (D2-D98/D50) for prostate HDR plan. Evaluate plan quality.
Calculate 95% CI for mean dwell position deviation (0.15 mm, SD=0.35, n=20) and process capability index (Cp with tolerance 1 mm).
Calculate dose-rate at point A using Manchester system loading pattern for tandem and ovoids.
Evaluate end-to-end test results: source strength 0.4%, dwell position 0.6 mm max, dwell time 0.2%, point dose 2.1%. Determine pass/fail per TG-59.
Calculate EUD for prostate HDR using power-law formula (a=-10) with given dose-volume distribution. Interpret result.
Calculate projected final EQD2 for bladder, rectum, sigmoid after fraction 4. Determine which OARs exceed 70 Gy tolerance.
Calculate 2D radial deviations and RMS from measured dwell positions. Evaluate against TG-59 tolerance.
Calculate dose-rate at 3 cm from tandem using inverse square law (1.5 Gy/sec at 1 cm). Total dose for 25 sec dwell time over 4 fractions. Compare to tolerance.
Calculate lead shielding thickness for HDR room: Ir-192 HVL=0.6 cm, max permissible 2 mGy/week, 10 Ci source, 3 m distance.
Calculate D90%, D100%, conformity index for APBI plan. Evaluate per ABS guidelines.
Calculate BED for three prostate HDR schedules (38/4, 36/4, 30/5) for tumor (ab=1.5) and normal tissue (ab=3). Determine best therapeutic ratio.
Evaluate measured dose (7.12 Gy) vs planned (7.00 Gy). Calculate % difference, total difference over 4 fractions, EQD2 difference, and clinical acceptability.

A monthly output check of the HDR afterloader reveals a 4.2% deviation from the expected dose rate. This exceeds the 3% tolerance level established by the department. Describe the investigation procedure, the potential causes of the deviation, the corrective actions needed, and the documentation and reporting requirements. How do you determine whether previously treated patients were affected?

A near-miss event occurred during brachytherapy when the wrong patient's plan was loaded onto the afterloader. The error was caught before treatment delivery. Describe the root cause analysis process, the system improvements needed to prevent recurrence, the reporting requirements, and how to communicate the event to staff without creating a culture of blame.

A center wants to implement statistical process control (SPC) for brachytherapy output measurements. Describe how to set up control charts for tracking HDR afterloader output, how to interpret control chart patterns (trends, shifts, cycles), what actions should be taken when out-of-control signals are detected, and how SPC differs from simple tolerance-based QA.

A brachytherapy center performs a failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) for its HDR treatment process. Identify the key failure modes in the brachytherapy workflow from patient setup through treatment delivery, calculate risk priority numbers for each failure mode, and describe the mitigation strategies for the highest-risk failure modes. How should the FMEA be updated and how often should it be reviewed?
Develop comprehensive QA program for HDR: acceptance testing, commissioning, daily/monthly/annual procedures, source exchange, and documentation requirements per TG-59.
Design QA protocol for brachytherapy planning: TPS commissioning, dose calculation verification, plan review, contouring QA, and export verification.
Develop source management QA: inventory system, chain of custody, decay verification, source strength measurement, source exchange procedures, and regulatory documentation.
Design emergency response for brachytherapy: stuck source, source exposure, contamination, applicator complications (perforation, hemorrhage), and notification requirements.
Develop QA for applicator placement: selection verification, placement quality metrics, imaging verification, reconstruction accuracy, and peer review process.
Design quality metrics dashboard: treatment delivery, plan quality, safety, patient experience, and operational efficiency metrics. Include display format and QI integration.
Develop peer review program: schedule, criteria/checklist, reviewer qualifications, documentation, conflict resolution, and outcome tracking.
Design equipment maintenance QA: preventive maintenance, corrective maintenance, performance monitoring, vendor requirements, spare parts, and downtime minimization.
Develop competency assessment: domains for all roles, assessment methods (observation, exams, simulation), frequency, remediation process, and documentation.
Design infection control for brachytherapy: sterile technique, antibiotic prophylaxis, applicator reprocessing/sterilization, OR requirements, and wound care protocols.
Develop radiation safety QA: ALARA implementation, personnel monitoring, area monitoring, license compliance, and training requirements per NRC regulations.
Design QI framework: project identification, PDSA cycles, data collection/analysis, intervention evaluation, sustainability, and reporting requirements.
Develop consent QA: content requirements, documentation standards, language access, pediatric considerations, emergency consent, and audit process.
Design treatment delivery QA: pre-treatment verification, intra-treatment monitoring, post-treatment documentation, fraction tracking, cumulative dose reporting, and error prevention.
Develop imaging QA: CT/MRI quality testing, applicator visualization verification, image fusion assessment, artifact management, and protocol optimization.
Design RCA protocol: incident classification, methodology (5-Why, fishbone), team composition, timeline, corrective action tracking, and learning dissemination.
Develop outcome tracking QA: metrics (local control, survival, toxicity), data collection (NCDB, registry), analysis methods, benchmarking, and reporting.
Design training QA: curriculum design, simulation requirements, competency milestones, continuing education, and documentation requirements.
Develop documentation completeness QA: required elements per phase, completeness audits, ICRU/GEC-ESTRO standards, electronic documentation, and compliance monitoring.
Design patient ID and safety verification: two-identifier process, site verification, timeout procedure, applicator/prescription verification, and error prevention.
Develop calculation QA: independent verification, TG-43 audit, point dose measurement, DVH verification, and cumulative dose calculation verification.
Design QA for transition to electronic documentation: system selection, workflow redesign, data migration, training, go-live support, and post-implementation monitoring.
Develop research data QA: data management plan, source data verification, database security, audit trails, data sharing protocols, and ICH-GCP compliance.
Design vendor management QA: qualification, SLAs, maintenance contracts, emergency service, spare parts management, and performance monitoring.
Develop tumor board QA: case selection, presentation standards, multidisciplinary participation, decision documentation, action tracking, and outcome correlation.

Review the following brachytherapy treatment plan for compliance with the ABS guidelines for cervical cancer brachytherapy. The prescription is 5.5 Gy per fraction x 4 fractions to point A. D2cc to the rectum is 3.5 Gy per fraction, and D2cc to the bladder is 4.0 Gy per fraction. Does this plan comply with ABS dose constraints? Identify any deviations and describe the appropriate action.

A center is performing brachytherapy without MRI guidance and using CT-only planning. Evaluate whether this practice complies with current GEC-ESTRO recommendations for cervical cancer brachytherapy. What are the documented limitations of CT-only planning, and what additional quality assurance measures should be implemented to mitigate these limitations?

Evaluate whether the following brachytherapy practice complies with state radiation safety regulations: The center treats HDR brachytherapy patients without a medical physicist present during treatment delivery, relying instead on trained radiation therapy technologists. The physicist is available by phone. Discuss the regulatory requirements for physicist presence during HDR treatments in different jurisdictions.

Review the informed consent documentation for a brachytherapy procedure. The current consent form mentions general risks of radiation therapy but does not specifically address brachytherapy-specific risks such as applicator-related complications, organ perforation, or the risk of fistula formation. Evaluate whether this consent form meets the standard of care for brachytherapy informed consent.

A multi-institutional clinical trial protocol requires brachytherapy dose reporting per ICRU 89 format. One of the participating centers has been reporting doses using ICRU 38 point-based format instead. Calculate the potential impact on data quality for the trial, describe the corrective actions needed, and explain how to prevent similar protocol deviations in the future.

Evaluate the following brachytherapy quality assurance program against the requirements of AAPM TG-56 and TG-59. The program includes daily equipment checks, monthly output measurements, annual comprehensive physics surveys, and treatment plan reviews. Identify any gaps in the QA program and recommend additions to ensure full compliance.

A center performs brachytherapy on pediatric patients but does not have specific pediatric dose constraints in its treatment planning system. The clinical team uses adult dose constraints for pediatric patients.
